title: Disclosure: "London Town"
author: transparent
bodyPreview: If we needed any further reassurance that we live in the best city in the world, it would be Disclosure easing us into their after-dark ode to "London Town" with a sexy saxophone. Our heroes of 24 hours ago ride back to open arms with more bottled-up samples on this smoky, spiraling, bass-heavy little underground dance jam. Not an airhorn in sight. (via Transparent) MP3: Disclosure: "London Town"

title: Alaskas: "The Truths of Tomorrow"
author: visitationrites
bodyPreview: Dillon James Rego is the sole constant in noise/rock/drone project Alaskas, ranging from purposefully crafted pop songs to loosely constructed ambience. Its defining characteristic is Rego’s voice, a distinctive yelp that he pushes into a cathartic wail on some tracks, a plaintive moan on others. “The Truths of Tomorrow”, from his upcoming D.I.V.A. LP, is a casual epic constructed from vocal loops

title: Power Animal: "Better Water"
author: weeklytapedeck
bodyPreview: Paul North sent "Better Water" from Power Animal our way, a song centered around a obvious-but-amazing reversed Willie Nelson sample. The Philly band slowly builds a creeping song around the legend's backwards croon with icy vocals and rubber-band drumming, sounding as if it was made to be placed in a warped koozie bought from the convenience store on the corner. author: getoffthecoast
bodyPreview: Throughout the '70s, Father's Children captivated DC with their bright brand of soulful pop. title: The Soft Moon Announces Total Decay EP
author: alteredzones
bodyPreview: San Francisco dark wavers The Soft Moon got our attention last year with their self-titled, zoned in debut on Captured Tracks, and now they're back with a new EP called Total Decay, which drops on Halloween (spoooooky!!). But don't be scared; sneak a peek at the album's title track. --Ric Leichtung, Altered Zones MP3: The Soft Moon: "Total Decay" Tweet

title: Dive: "Sometime (Heavenly Beat Edit)"
author: alteredzones
bodyPreview: Last week we dropped "Sometime," the premiere recording from Brooklyn's Dive-- a Can-inspired four-piece fronted by Beach Fossils guitarist Cole Smith. The track sounded like a decidedly grayer version of Smith's other band, with downbeat post-punk leanings and more strongly ringing guitars. title: Black Eagle Child: "Cycle to the Moon"
author: alteredzones
bodyPreview: Following his well received full-length Lobelia, Black Eagle Child's Michael Jantz recorded 12 whole inches of beautiful, field recording-backed guitar loops and named the thing Pages On A Plane. "Cycle to the Moon" grounds its melodies in some krauty percussion that I've never heard from BEC before, but the repetition brings out a buoyancy easily unnoticed in his ambient-folk output. --Ian Pearso

title: Light Asylum: "Dark Allies" (Joey Hansom & Dickey Doo Remix)
author: alteredzones
bodyPreview: Light Asylum's "Dark Allies" may already be one of the most macabre feel good anthems of 2010-2011, but the Berlin-based DJ duo of Joey Hansom and Dickey Doo have gone and taken it one step further with this vaudevillian edit of the single, just in time for Halloween. Don't worry, it's not another Monster Mash-Up, although the bassline is chromatic in the most seasonally appropriate of ways. --Emi

title: Steve Hauschildt: "Already Replaced"
author: alteredzones
bodyPreview: The Emeralds synth man's last song, "Batteries May Drain" might've made you worry about the mortality of your everyday portable electrochemical cells, but with this new MP3, you don't have to live your life worrying anymore. Hauschildt consoles us with a song of regenerative introspection in "Already Replaced," taken from his latest, Tragedy & Geometry, which dropped yesterday on CD and double LP
